clue.text: Say something tactless and lose a real friend

parts.note: to lose something is to let it fall, to drop it
a brick is old-fashioned British slang for a dependable, generous friend

explanation.surface: A blunder of speech that costs someone a true friendship.
explanation.walkthrough: BRICK, as in 'you're a brick', is dated British praise for a loyal, helpful person.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom, chiefly British, for making an embarrassing indiscreet remark.

clue.text: Delicacy isn't commonly penetrating outskirts of Dudley

indicators.note: penetrating means going into, so one piece sits inside the other
the outskirts of a word are its outer letters, first and last

parts.note: ain't is the colloquial, non-standard form of isn't

explanation.surface: A grumble that a fine treat doesn't reach the edge of a Midlands town.
explanation.walkthrough: Dudley is a town in the West Midlands; only its outer letters D and Y are used, with AINT between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A dainty is a small tasty morsel or titbit, a delicacy to eat.

clue.text: Rouse stiffly off and on and become rigid

indicators.note: off and on tells us to skip one letter, take the next, and so on through the words

explanation.surface: Someone roused from sleep keeps stiffening up, a picture of joints seizing.
explanation.walkthrough: Starting with the second letter of 'Rouse stiffly' and taking every other one gives O, S, S, I, F, Y.
explanation.definitionFit: To ossify is literally to turn into bone, and figuratively to harden or grow inflexible.

clue.text: Welsh factories redeveloped directly

indicators.note: redeveloped suggests the letters are rebuilt into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Industrial sites in Wales have been regenerated in a straight line.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for the shortest straight-line distance, taking the most direct route.

clue.text: Civil War soldier perhaps or a recent revolutionary

indicators.note: revolutionary hints at overturning, so the letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A historical soldier, or else someone who has just joined a rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or a recent' looks like an alternative to the soldier, but those nine letters are the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dresses up to stage historical battles, such as those of the English or American Civil War, is an example.

clue.text: Policeman points and carries on

parts.note: cop is slang for a police officer
E and S, east and south, are compass points

explanation.surface: An officer points the way and keeps going.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean manages to keep going or deals with matters despite difficulty.

clue.text: Lie alongside a capsized unwieldy vessel

indicators.note: a capsized boat is upside down, so in a down light this word is read backwards

parts.note: a tub is a slow, clumsy boat

explanation.surface: An overturned clumsy boat lies next to something.
explanation.definitionFit: To abut is to border on or adjoin, to lie next to something.

clue.text: Clever clogs support popular TV

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
in means fashionable or popular
the box is a colloquial name for the television

explanation.surface: A smart person backs well-liked television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clever clogs' is British slang for a know-all.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British terms for a very clever, intellectual person.

clue.text: This lot going about in a frenzy, heading off for London

indicators.note: going about means surrounding, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: these refers to this lot, the group here

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: running amok is behaving in a frenzy

explanation.surface: A frantic group sets out for the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading off' trims only the frenzy word, and 'going about' puts the result inside the group word. 'The Smoke' is an old British nickname for London.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional nickname for the capital, from its once-sooty air.

clue.text: Skip how to find use for a nut?

definitions.meaning: to skip is to run away or abscond

definitions.text: how to find use for a nut?
definitions.meaning: a nut is useless without a bolt, so one makes a bolt to go with it

explanation.surface: A practical DIY question about putting a spare nut to use.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for running off quickly to escape, which is what skipping means here.

clue.text: Gusset in cardigan and jumper Terry Wogan originally let out

indicators.note: let out means these letters are released from the word

parts.note: a twinset is a matching cardigan and jumper worn together

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of each name

explanation.surface: A broadcaster's knitwear has had its seams let out with an extra panel.
explanation.walkthrough: Terry Wogan was a much-loved BBC broadcaster; his initials T and W leave TWINSET.
explanation.definitionFit: A gusset is a piece of material set into a garment to strengthen or enlarge it.

clue.text: Delinquent pedals around an English seafront

indicators.note: around means the scrambled letters go round the next piece
delinquent means wayward, so the letters stray into a new order

explanation.surface: A cycling hooligan rides round an English seaside promenade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delinquent' scrambles the six letters to ESPLAD; 'around' wraps that round the article, and the English abbreviation goes last.
explanation.definitionFit: An esplanade is a long open level walkway, typically along the shore of a resort.

clue.text: Stout turned cheese into silky stuff

indicators.note: turned means the word is read backwards

parts.note: stout means fat
feta is a Greek cheese

explanation.surface: A sour stout beer and cheese somehow become a fine fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stout' suggests the dark beer, but here it is the adjective, FAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a crisp lustrous fabric of silk or similar fibre.

clue.text: Bird dips into quantity of money that's hidden in chest

indicators.note: dips into means the bird goes inside the other piece

parts.note: a sum is an amount of money
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A bird raids a stash of cash concealed in a trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chest' looks like a box for treasure, but it is the body's chest.
explanation.definitionFit: The sternum is the breastbone, lying inside the front of the ribcage.

clue.text: Author's head failing to generate ideas

parts.note: an author is a writer, here with the possessive
block is slang for the head, as in 'knock his block off'

explanation.surface: A novelist's mind has dried up, producing nothing new.
explanation.definitionFit: The name for the condition of a novelist unable to produce new work or think of material.

clue.text: Production of Lear outside picks up in run-through

indicators.note: outside means the rearranged letters surround the other piece
a production remakes something, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: to pick up a sound is to hear it

explanation.surface: A staging of King Lear is overheard during a practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Production of' turns the king's name into REAL, and 'outside' splits it round the word for picks up.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a practice performance before the real one.

clue.text: Pride drooling — lion's first to go out and last to tuck in

indicators.text: lion's first to go out and last to tuck in
indicators.note: the lion's opening letter is removed and its final letter is put in its place

parts.note: slobbery means wet with drool

explanation.surface: A slavering lion leaves and returns, conjuring a pride of lions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pride' suggests lions, but it is the definition in its sense of haughtiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Snobbery is a form of pride: looking down on those thought socially inferior.

clue.text: Carrying hose

definitions.meaning: a shop carrying an item has it in stock
hose is a collective name for leg coverings worn on the feet and legs

explanation.definitionFit: A shop keeping goods on sale is doing this; separately, the word names a knitted leg garment.

clue.text: Memorably observe eminent person pinching contents of till

parts.note: to note is to observe

indicators.note: pinching means holding the next piece inside, as if stealing it

parts.note: a worthy is a notable or important person

indicators.note: the contents of a word are its inner letters

explanation.surface: Watching a dignitary steal from the cash register, a memorable sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adverbs describe something done in a way worth remembering or remarking on.

clue.text: 'Une route secondaire' in France maybe

parts.note: une is French for a
a secondary road is, in British terms

explanation.surface: A French phrase for a minor road, as it might appear on a map in France.
explanation.walkthrough: British roads are graded A, B and so on; a B road is a minor one.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in France is one example of being overseas, in a foreign country.

clue.text: One fat fly starts off smartly

indicators.note: starts off means the opening letter of each word is dropped

explanation.surface: A single plump fly takes off sharply.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping O, F and F from 'One fat fly' leaves NE, AT, LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Neatly and smartly both describe something done tidily and with precision.

clue.text: Reserves support look good

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Reserve players back a promising showing.
explanation.definitionFit: A backlog is an accumulation of things kept or awaiting attention, a store in reserve.

clue.text: School waiving rights for third grade

indicators.note: waiving means giving something up, so these letters are removed

parts.note: a grammar is a grammar school
R is the abbreviation for right, so rights is two of them

explanation.surface: A school drops entitlements for its youngest year group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Third grade' looks like a school year, but it is the third Greek letter used as a grade.
explanation.definitionFit: The third letter of the Greek alphabet, used for a third-class mark or grade.

clue.text: Very loud seaman in the drink? Gracious!

indicators.note: in means the first pieces are placed inside the drink

parts.note: ale is a drink
ff, fortissimo, is the musical direction for very loud
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A noisy sailor falls into the sea, prompting an exclamation of surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The drink' is slang for the sea, but here it is beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Affable and gracious both mean courteous, friendly and kind; the exclamation mark is surface dressing.

clue.text: One's got it all over with tragic demise (RIP)

indicators.note: tragic suggests something wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A heavily punctuated epitaph for someone who had it all before an unhappy death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got it all over' sounds like boasting superiority, but it means covering the whole body.
explanation.definitionFit: Everyone has an outer skin layer covering the whole body.

clue.text: Chick might settle on this jumper with short sleeves

parts.note: a roo, a kangaroo, is a jumper

indicators.note: sleeves are the outside of a word, so its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A girl settles on a jumper with short sleeves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' looks like a sweater, as 'sleeves' supports, but it is a kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: A perch where birds, including young ones, settle to rest.

clue.text: Characters in Tokyo gangs attaining spiritual discipline

indicators.note: characters in means the letters are found inside the following words

explanation.surface: Japanese gang members take up a meditative practice.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu practice of breathing, posture and meditation aimed at spiritual union.

clue.text: Give up present title for 24 hours?

definitions.meaning: to give up is to stop working, finish for now
to give a twenty-four hour period its name is to label it a day

explanation.surface: An offer to give up a title for a single day.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for stopping work or ending an activity, which is what giving up means here.
